messages:
maya: Heads-up — brought up the quantized v2 judge in the eval-runner smoke job and saw a spike in tie-break flips vs v1. Not huge but consistent across 3 datasets.

sasha: ugh. is this on the judge model only or the whole pipeline?

maya: isolated to judge only. main gen model unchanged. I ran a quick A/B: v1 judge -> 2.1% ties, v2-quant -> 7.9% ties on `sensebench_small`.

kevin: can you paste the runner config you used? we might be batching differently with quantization.

maya: sure — used the smoke runner job:```
runner: eval-smoke
judge_model: redwood/judge-v2-quant:dev
seed: 42
max_tokens: 256
batch_size: 8
metric: pairwise_consensus
ci_gate: false
```

liam: logs from the CI job show a bunch of transient timeouts hitting the judge subprocess right before tie detections. snippet: `WARN judge: response truncated (timeout=1500ms)`

kevin: timeouts could bias toward shorter outputs from the quantized judge. shorter output -> less context for tie-breaker heuristics -> more ties. try bumping timeout to 3s for the smoke job.

maya: tried that — tie rate drops to ~5.2% but still > v1. So timeout explains part but not all.

eval-bot: perf/regression check: judge-v2-quant vs judge-v1 -> tie_flip_rate +5.7pp, kappa -0.06, p<0.01 (n=1200).

sasha: kappa drop is concerning. could be calibration shift. do we have calibration plots?

maya: uploaded quick calibration PNG to the thread (link) — v2 skewed toward mid-confidence scores around 0.45-0.55. v1 had more mass near 0.7/0.8 for winners.

kevin: two-pronged: 1) short-term: add deterministic tie-break fallback (lexicographic + prefer v1 on ties) for canary traffic; 2) long-term: run a recalibration pass (temp scaling or isotonic) on judge logits post-quantization.

eva: +1 on dashboard alerts. can someone add a tile in Redwood Console for `judge_tie_rate` and an alert when delta vs baseline > 3pp? we need to catch this in continuous eval.

liam: I can add the alert. PR: #4983 — adds a tile and alert rule, also wires the smoke job to emit `judge_tie_rate` metric.

maya: thanks. also flagged an issue in the runner: when `ci_gate: false` we accidentally skip the full adjudication step. that affected our smoke sampling. filing a quick PR to ensure handoff path is exercised even in smoke mode.

kevin: good catch. might explain some of the behaviour if the fallback adjudicator wasn't exercised.

sasha: for judge selection, propose we add an internal eval that runs quantized judge + unquantized judge ensemble as the tie-breaker for 1k samples for 48h during canary. if quantized disagrees > 4pp, abort rollout.

maya: sounds reasonable. I'll write the runner job and test locally. putting a note to run on the 3 priority datasets: sensebench_small, safety-probe, and longform-coherence.

ops-bot: deploy initiated by maya for branch `eval-runner/ensure-handoff` at 2025-02-14T15:23:00Z :rocket:

liam: CI job for PR #4983 failed once due to flakiness in the smoke harness. logs show `AssertionError: expected adjudicated_count > 0`. looks like the handoff skip bug reproduced.

maya: fixing now, pushing patch. will rerun full smoke with: `BATCH=8 TIMEOUT_MS=3000 ./run_smoke.sh --datasets sensebench_small,safety-probe,longform`

kevin: once fixed, let's run a calibration sweep: temp in [1.0,1.2,1.5], isotonic. compute tie_rate and kappa and pick the minimal loss under our cost function (tie_penalty=2, kappa_weight=1).

sasha: also add a small synthetic test for tie-breaking edge cases (palindromes, equal token probs) to the eval unit tests so future quantize passes don't regress silently.

maya: added unit test locally, pushing. will re-run and post updated eval-bot summary when complete.

eval-bot: queued comparison job (id: 20250214-ev-77). expected runtime ~45m. will post results here.

eva: great work. once we have numbers, let's sync with product about rollout gating. short note to pm-team would help. :thumbsup:
